entries.rationale: Tauri Quick Menu owns live windows, saved-window restore, status, legal gating, and stop-all.
Native Tauri menu construction replaces the old shell template.
The signed Tauri updater and its failure state replace electron-updater.
The Tauri update controller retains the automatic-update preference and the signed updater contract.
Window state events and UI behavior remain covered without Electron.
Tauri native menus restore Edit, zoom, fullscreen, window actions, and toolbar preference.
Graphics-driven restart prompts and the renderer restart API are retired with application-owned Chromium graphics settings.
Rust launch effects and System WebView configuration replace Electron launch options.
Focused Tauri tests now verify shared display-host lifecycle, native surface switching, layout, and the scoped tab strip.
Authenticated single-instance activation is implemented and unit-tested in Rust.
Electron debugger automation is explicitly retired; native trusted-input attestation is the supported path.
Browser actions now cross the bounded Rust effect boundary into native System WebViews.
Electron Builder is retired and Tauri bundle configuration is authoritative.
The Tauri runtime source test verifies the bounded native effect executor and its recovery paths without Electron.
Electron Vite entry points are retired; the Tauri renderer build is the only frontend build.
System WebView capability, recovery, and diagnostics are emitted from Rust.
Font, macro badge, and workspace appearance settings persist in SQLite while retired graphics and proxy fields are read only for migration.
Compatibility decisions remain in Rust and resolve only to System WebViews.
Game persistence and product behavior remain covered across Rust and renderer tests.
Untrusted global Chromium diagnostics are replaced by measured per-game WebView2 or WKWebView compatibility reports.
Current macro runtime tests exercise the bounded overlay path while Rust unit tests own held-key state and release semantics.
Workspace storage remains in the shared SQLite repository.
Legal acceptance and current release versions are validated in Rust and renderer documents.
Current runtime-session tests cover the user-facing recovery surface while Rust unit tests own structured log persistence and capture.
The AppKit controller now receives bounded state/actions through Rust FFI and a Tauri NSWindow.
WKWebView lifecycle, security, input, and content geometry remain native.
The same overlay runtime is injected by each native role WebView.
DOM interaction coverage is restored against the shell-neutral overlay runtime.
Macro settings remain in SQLite and the current settings UI.
Macro CRUD remains in the Rust repository and renderer workflow.
Ready-before-show, close-to-hide, Dock reopen, and startup failure behavior are Tauri-owned.
Document-start scripts and scoped bridges are installed by native Tauri WebView builders.
Portable import/export and migration remain Rust-owned and transactionally tested.
Role metadata and browser-directory operations remain Rust-owned.
The runtime tab strip receives per-game icon data and has a local fallback marker.
Crash recovery, dormant windows, and per-tab audio state remain in the Tauri runtime.
Current runtime tests cover native handle release, restore state, and the user-facing shutdown and recovery controls.
The Electron macOS fallback preload is retired; AppKit tabs are reached through Rust FFI.
The Windows local tab strip uses a scoped Tauri command instead of preload IPC.
The shell-neutral action and tooltip contract was restored at the same path.
Fullscreen toolbar and overlay preferences persist in Rust scalar state.
Macro scheduling, held-key release, and queue semantics remain Rust-owned.
The generic Electron webContents sender is retired; scoped typed Tauri events are used instead.
Tauri release and local package builds explicitly use macOS ad-hoc signing and strip notarization credentials.
The Tauri shell parity suite covers the single-instance activation wiring backed by Rust unit tests.
The main window stays hidden until two renderer frames complete and has a bundled failure page.
The native runtime suite verifies that compatibility surfaces remain isolated platform System WebViews.
Per-role isolated WebViews and non-reloading tab windows are owned by the Rust/Tauri runtime.
Preview identity and transitional entry points are retired; Tauri Stable is the product shell.
Legacy-to-stable data-root migration now has transactional Rust tests and production startup wiring.
Current typed contract tests verify bounded renderer actions while Rust and the Tauri bridge dispatch authoritative core commands.
General automation targets are retired; bounded native input and recovery attestations remain.
The Tauri Quick Menu restores per-display and per-saved-window actions.
WebView2 probing, security, input, and recovery remain native Rust platform code.
Tauri child WebViews replace the removed N-API surface wrapper.
Display enumeration, hotplug reconciliation, and selection remain covered.
Rust coordinates workspace launch and Tauri preserves pending display-selection requests.
